paper_id: Alleviating Hallucinations from Knowledge Misalignment in Large Language Models via Selective Abstention Learning
title: Alleviating Hallucinations from Knowledge Misalignment in Large Language Models via Selective Abstention Learning
motivation: LLMs hallucinate when fine-tuning introduces new factual knowledge not in model's parametric memory, forcing fabrication.
problem_framing: Knowledge misalignment between pretraining and SFT makes model fit unknown samples, leading to overconfident wrong answers.
key_insight: Introduce [REJ] token to absorb uncertainty; model can choose to abstain instead of blindly fitting ground truth.
method_signature: Abstention tuning + abstention-aware beam search decoding using [REJ] probability as uncertainty penalty.
evaluation_criteria: Factuality accuracy (short-form QA), FActScore/F1 (long-form QA), AlpacaEval/IFEval (instruction following).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: POPULAR baseline struggles in long-form QA; ratio-based confidence capture is 'simple' and may miss other uncertainty patterns.
evidence_for_taste: rather than blindly assigning high probability
significantly correlation between REJ and factuality
thinking_moves: 把未知样本问题从数据过滤重新定义为训练目标修改
用特殊token吸收不确定性,给模型一个'拒绝回答'的选项
训练信号转化为解码约束,形成从学习到推理的一致性
先在小规模数据验证因果机制,再扩展到复杂生成任务
